title: Reduce capacity-planner entanglement and slim node lifecycle surface
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: The capacity planner and node lifecycle controller are tightly coupled: policy evaluation, provisioning side-effects, and node state transitions are implemented in a single reconciler. This causes long reconcile latencies (>200ms median), frequent deadlocks during upgrades, and an opaque control flow that blocks telemetry and graceful evacuation.

Goal: Reduce coupling by extracting a minimal lifecycle adapter surface, move policy evaluation into a read-only planner stage, and replace the central lease cache with an epoch-based lock-free reader to improve concurrent reconciles. This ticket covers design, implementation, perf benchmarks and a safe rollout plan.

Scope: planner disentanglement, node adapter API, lease cache replacement, unit+integration tests, e2e perf runs, one canary rollout on staging GPU pool. Excludes autoscaler UI changes and billing integration (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Median reconciler CPU time reduced by >=30% in synthetic reconcile workload
End-to-end request-to-binding latency improved (median) by >=20% for provisioning flows
No increase in reconciler error rate in canary pool over 72h
All existing unit/integration tests pass; add tests for new lifecycle adapter contract
Migration path documented and automated with a rollback toggle
tasks: Design lifecycle adapter interface and public contract (non-blocking API)
Implement read-only policy evaluation stage in capacity planner service
Replace central lease cache with epoch-based reader cache implementation
Refactor reconcile loop to invoke lifecycle adapter and planner separately
Upgrade k8s client from v0.24.x to v0.27.x; validate list/watch behavior
Add unit/integration tests and a synthetic reconcile benchmark harness
Run staging canary on small GPU pool and collect perf/telemetry over 72h
Prepare rollout playbook and feature flag for safe rollback
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag -> run in isolated staging pool for 72h -> compare reconcile latency, error budget, and eviction behavior -> enable in incremental production rings (10%, 50%, 100%) with automated monitoring checks and automatic rollback on policy violations.
migration_steps: Deploy new planner binary with feature flag disabled
Run compatibility mode where planner publishes a read-only snapshot but existing lifecycle controller still handles side-effects
Enable lifecycle adapter in staging pool and validate behavior for 72h
Switch production rings with 10% traffic and monitor metrics for 24h each step
If rollback triggered, flip feature flag and observe systems return to baseline
test_plan: Unit: adapter contract, cache epoch transitions, k8s client upgrade mocks
Integration: full reconcile loop with simulated node flapping, provisioning races
E2E: synthetic workload matching production sequence length and burst patterns
Performance: run benchmark harness comparing baseline vs. refactor under identical load
Chaos: introduce transient k8s API latency and verify graceful degradation
risks: Behavioral regressions from k8s client upgrade (watch semantics changed)
Race between old and new caches during rollout causing double allocations
Unobserved side-effects where lifecycle adapter omits a subtle heuristic used by older reconciler
Insufficient test coverage for rare node eviction edge-cases
notes: Prefer non-blocking, idempotent adapter operations; side-effects should be queued by a separate worker when possible.
We will keep a short-lived compatibility shim to reduce blast radius during rollout.
Benchmark harness will run on the same GPU instance types as staging to avoid skew.
If we detect >5% increase in 99th percentile latency in any rollout ring, we will automatically rollback and open an incident for post-mortem.
